notes.choicesExplained: B: FINRA’s rule treats occasional transcription, confirmed by a registered person before entry, as not accepting an order. C: accepting orders requires registration.
notes.explanation: The registered person confirmed the details with the customer before entering the order, which is the condition.
notes.source: Federal Register doc. 2017-07046 (2017-04-10), SEC notice of FINRA’s proposed consolidated registration rules, section N
notes.evidence: an associated person is not accepting a customer order where occasionally, when an appropriately registered person is unavailable, the associated person transcribes the order details and the registered person contacts the customer to confirm the order details before entering the order.

notes.front: What can FINRA staff compel under FINRA Rule 8210?
notes.back: A member or associated person to produce documents, give testimony, or supply written responses or electronic data in an investigation, complaint, examination or proceeding.
notes.explanation: Staff can also inspect and copy the member’s or person’s books, records and accounts on any matter involved.
notes.source: Federal Register doc. 2012-30049 (2012-12-13), SEC order approving amendments to FINRA Rule 8210, section III
notes.evidence: Current FINRA Rule 8210 confers on FINRA staff authority to compel a member, person associated with a member, or other person subject to FINRA's jurisdiction, to produce documents, provide testimony, or supply written responses or electronic data in connection with an investigation, complaint, examination or adjudicatory proceeding.
notes.validAsOf: 2012-12-13 · FINRA Rule 8210 as amended in 2012; later amendments not checked

notes.front: A representative left his firm six months ago. FINRA sends him a Rule 8210 request for testimony, and he ignores it because he is no longer registered. Is he in the clear?
notes.back: No: the rule reaches former associated persons still within FINRA’s jurisdiction, and failing to testify violates it.
notes.choices:
A) No
B) Yes: the rule applies only to current members
C) Yes, unless he is later charged with fraud
notes.choicesExplained: B: the rule covers former associated persons subject to FINRA’s jurisdiction under its By-Laws. C: failing to provide testimony is itself a violation.
notes.explanation: Rule 8210(c) makes a failure to provide information or testimony a violation of the rule.
notes.source: Federal Register doc. 2012-30049 (2012-12-13), SEC order approving amendments to FINRA Rule 8210, section I
notes.evidence: FINRA Rule 8210 applies to all members, associated persons, and other persons over whom FINRA has jurisdiction, including former associated persons subject to FINRA's jurisdiction as described in the FINRA By-Laws.
notes.validAsOf: 2012-12-13 · FINRA Rule 8210 as amended in 2012; later amendments not checked

notes.front: Under the Exchange Act’s criminal penalty section, what filing conduct can lead to prosecution?
notes.back: Wilfully and knowingly making a materially false or misleading statement in any application, report or document required to be filed.
notes.explanation: This includes statements in applications to a self-regulatory organisation to become associated with a member.
notes.source: 15 U.S.C. 78ff (Exchange Act s. 32), penalties, subsection (a), subsection (a)
notes.evidence: any person who willfully and knowingly makes, or causes to be made, any statement in any application, report, or document required to be filed under this chapter or any rule or regulation thereunder

notes.front: To hide a client’s losses before an audit, an operations manager knowingly alters figures in a report the firm must file under the Exchange Act. What exposure does this create?
notes.back: Criminal liability for wilfully and knowingly making a false statement in a required report: up to $5 million and 20 years.
notes.choices:
A) Criminal liability for a false required report
B) None, if the numbers are corrected later
C) Only a Regulation M violation
notes.choicesExplained: B: the offence is making the false statement wilfully and knowingly. C: Regulation M concerns bidding during distributions.
notes.explanation: Knowingly falsifying a required report falls within the criminal penalty section.
notes.source: 15 U.S.C. 78ff (Exchange Act s. 32), penalties, subsection (a), subsection (a)
notes.evidence: shall upon conviction be fined not more than $5,000,000, or imprisoned not more than 20 years, or both

notes.front: Under Rule 15c1-3, what may a broker-dealer not say about its SEC registration?
notes.back: That it means the SEC has passed on or approved its financial standing, business or conduct, or the merits of any security.
notes.explanation: The rule defines such a representation as a manipulative, deceptive or other fraudulent device.
notes.evidence: the failure of the Commission to deny or revoke such registration, indicates in any way that the Commission has passed upon or approved the financial standing, business, or conduct of such registered broker, dealer or municipal securities dealer or the merits of any security

notes.front: What does MSRB Rule G-17 require of dealers in their municipal securities activities?
notes.back: To deal fairly with all persons, including municipal issuers, and not engage in any deceptive, dishonest or unfair practice.
notes.explanation: MSRB interpretive notices apply this duty to underwriters’ dealings with issuers.
notes.source: Federal Register doc. 2019-17047 (2019-08-09), SEC notice of MSRB’s proposed restatement of its Rule G-17 interpretive notice, section 1
notes.evidence: Rule G-17 requires that, in the conduct of municipal securities activities, brokers, dealers and municipal securities dealers (collectively, ``dealers'') deal fairly with all persons, including municipal entity issuers, and not engage in any deceptive, dishonest or unfair practice.

notes.front: Which MSRB rule stops a dealer from sharing, directly or indirectly, in the profits or losses of a municipal securities transaction with or for a customer?
notes.back: MSRB Rule G-25(c).
notes.explanation: It is the municipal counterpart of the ban on sharing in customer accounts.
notes.source: Federal Register doc. 2019-17047 (2019-08-09), SEC notice of MSRB’s proposed restatement of its Rule G-17 interpretive notice, Implementation Guidance
notes.evidence: MSRB Rule G-25(c) precluding a dealer from directly or indirectly sharing in the profits or losses of a transaction in municipal securities with or for a customer
